reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch resolve the tension by separating the deed from the motive, holding that Jehu's slaughter fulfilled God's command even as his own ambition made it guilt.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen frames Jehu's slaughter, though prophet-instigated, as a crime whose horror still stood behind Hosea's condemnation a century later.

quotes.text: We can scarcely say the same of Jehu, the murderer, instigated by the prophets, of the house of Ahab (2Kings ix. 10). … the people, which he despised (x. 9), stood motionless and horrified at the sight of the crimes which came so quickly one after another; even a hundred years afterwards the horror at the massacre of Jezreel still lived (Hosea i. 4).
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on 2 Kings 9:7 and Hosea 1:4.

sides.snippet: You shall strike the house of Ahab your master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets
sides.verseText: You shall strike the house of Ahab your master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Yahweh, at the hand of Jezebel.

sides.snippet: I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu
sides.verseText: Yahweh said to him, \"Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Jehu, and will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
